verses.original: Κἀγώ ἀδελφοί οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλ’ ὡς σαρκίνοις ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ
verses.transliteration: Kagō adelphoi ouk ēdynēthēn lalēsai hymin hōs pneumatikois all’ hōs sarkinois hōs nēpiois en Christō
verses.literal: Brothers I could not address you as spiritual but as worldly as infants in Christ

verses.original: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα οὐ βρῶμα οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε Ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε
verses.transliteration: gala hymas epotisa ou brōma oupō gar edynasthe All’ oude eti nyn dynasthe
verses.literal: I gave you milk not solid food for you were not yet ready for solid food In fact you are still not ready

verses.original: ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε
verses.transliteration: eti gar sarkikoi este hopou gar en hymin zēlos kai eris ouchi sarkikoi este kai kata anthrōpon peripateite
verses.literal: for you are still worldly For since there is jealousy and dissension among you are you not worldly Are you not walking in the way of man

verses.original: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου ἕτερος δέ Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε
verses.transliteration: hotan gar legē tis Egō men eimi Paulou heteros de Egō Apollō ouk anthrōpoi este
verses.literal: For when one of you says I follow Paul and another I follow Apollos are you not mere men

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος διάκονοι δι’ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν
verses.transliteration: Ti oun estin Apollōs ti de estin Paulos diakonoi di’ hōn episteusate kai hekastō hōs ho Kyrios edōken
verses.literal: What then is Apollos And what is Paul They are servants through whom you believed as the Lord has assigned to each his role

verses.original: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν ἀλλὰ ὁ Θεὸς ηὔξανεν
verses.transliteration: egō ephyteusa Apollōs epotisen alla ho Theos ēuxanen
verses.literal: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it but God made it grow

verses.original: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων ἀλλ’ ὁ αὐξάνων Θεός
verses.transliteration: hōste oute ho phyteuōn estin ti oute ho potizōn all’ ho auxanōn Theos
verses.literal: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything but only God who makes things grow

verses.original: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον
verses.transliteration: ho phyteuōn de kai ho potizōn hen eisin hekastos de ton idion misthon lēmpsetai kata ton idion kopon
verses.literal: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose and each will be rewarded . . . . . . . . . according to his own labor

verses.original: Θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί Θεοῦ γεώργιον Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε
verses.transliteration: Theou gar esmen synergoi Theou geōrgion Theou oikodomē este
verses.literal: For we are God’s fellow workers you are God’s field God’s building

verses.original: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ
verses.transliteration: Kata tēn charin tou Theou tēn dotheisan moi hōs sophos architektōn themelion ethēka allos de epoikodomei hekastos de blepetō pōs epoikodomei
verses.literal: By the grace God has given me I laid a foundation as an expert builder and someone else is building on it But each one must be careful how he builds

verses.original: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός
verses.transliteration: themelion gar allon oudeis dynatai theinai para ton keimenon hos estin Iēsous Christos
verses.literal: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid which is Jesus Christ

verses.original: Εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσόν ἄργυρον λίθους τιμίους ξύλα χόρτον καλάμην
verses.transliteration: Ei de tis epoikodomei epi ton themelion chryson argyron lithous timious xyla chorton kalamēn
verses.literal: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold silver precious stones wood hay or straw

verses.original: ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει
verses.transliteration: hekastou to ergon phaneron genēsetai hē gar hēmera dēlōsei hoti en pyri apokalyptetai kai hekastou to ergon hopoion estin to pyr auto dokimasei
verses.literal: his workmanship will be evident because the Day will bring it to light It will be revealed with fire and the fire will prove the quality . . . of each man’s work

verses.original: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν μισθὸν λήμψεται
verses.transliteration: ei tinos to ergon menei ho epoikodomēsen misthon lēmpsetai
verses.literal: If what he has built survives he will receive a reward

verses.original: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται ζημιωθήσεται αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός
verses.transliteration: ei tinos to ergon katakaēsetai zēmiōthēsetai autos de sōthēsetai houtōs de hōs dia pyros
verses.literal: If it is burned up he will suffer loss He himself will be saved but only as if through the flames

verses.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς Θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν οἰκεῖ
verses.transliteration: Ouk oidate hoti naos Theou este kai to Pneuma tou Theou en hymin oikei
verses.literal: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple and that - God’s Spirit dwells in you

verses.original: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φθείρει φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς
verses.transliteration: ei tis ton naon tou Theou phtheirei phtherei touton ho Theos ho gar naos tou Theou hagios estin hoitines este hymeis
verses.literal: If anyone destroys God’s temple God will destroy him for God’s temple is holy and you are that temple

verses.original: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ μωρὸς γενέσθω ἵνα γένηται σοφός
verses.transliteration: Mēdeis heauton exapatatō ei tis dokei sophos einai en hymin en tō aiōni toutō mōros genesthō hina genētai sophos
verses.literal: Let no one deceive himself If any of you thinks he is wise in this age he should become a fool so that he may become wise

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐστιν γέγραπται γάρ Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: hē gar sophia tou kosmou toutou mōria para tō Theō estin gegraptai gar Ho drassomenos tous sophous en tē panourgia autōn
verses.literal: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight . . . . . . As it is written He catches the wise in their craftiness

verses.original: καὶ πάλιν Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι
verses.transliteration: kai palin Kyrios ginōskei tous dialogismous tōn sophōn hoti eisin mataioi
verses.literal: And again The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile

verses.original: Ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Hōste mēdeis kauchasthō en anthrōpois panta gar hymōn estin
verses.literal: Therefore stop boasting in men All things are yours

verses.original: εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα πάντα ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: eite Paulos eite Apollōs eite Kēphas eite kosmos eite zōē eite thanatos eite enestōta eite mellonta panta hymōn
verses.literal: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future All of them belong to you

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ Χριστὸς δὲ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: hymeis de Christou Christos de Theou
verses.literal: and you belong to Christ and Christ belongs to God
